newsitem.title: DUBAI: Defeated Kurd leader Talabani vows to fight on.
newsitem.headline: Defeated Kurd leader Talabani vows to fight on.

text.p: The leader of a Kurdish faction defeated by Iraq-backed rivals vowed on Friday to fight on and denied receiving Iranian support.

"We believe we should stay in our country and continue the struggle in cities and the countryside," Jalal Talabani, leader of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), said in a interview broadcast by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC).
"I do not think the PUK has been defeated...It has lost a battle, but the war continues and armed struggle goes on across Kurdistan," Talabani said in the taped interview.
Talabani was speaking on Friday in an area in northern Iraq about 5 km (3 miles) from the Iranian border, said the radio's Persian Service, monitored in Dubai.
The BBC said Talabani also spoke to a gathering of about 2,000 PUK guerrillas, vowing counter-attacks soon.

PUK guerrillas were defeated in a 10-day drive through northern Iraq by the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP). The KDP campaign began on August 31 with the taking of the Iraqi Kurdish capital Arbil, and ended last Monday with the seizure of Sulaimaniya.
"If Iran had given us anti-tank arms (Iraqi President) Saddam (Hussein) could not have taken Arbil...If Iran were helping us the situation would have been different now," he said.
Iraq said its attack on Arbil, which prompted U.S. missile strikes on southern Iraq, was aimed at backing the KDP against the PUK and Iran. Tehran denies backing the PUK.
"I hold America responsible for the Arbil defeat. If America had held its promises (of protection) Saddam Hussein would not have been able to capture Arbil," he said, speaking in Persian.
Washington should have bombed Iraqi forces around Arbil instead of hitting southern Iraq, Talabani added.
Tens of tousands of Kurds have fled KDP forces, and the United Nations refugee agency said on Friday it was launching an emergency operation for up to 40,000 Kurds who have crossed into Iran.
Iraq has issued a general amnesty for Kurds and the KDP has issued its own amnesty to PUK forces. But Kurdish refugees in Iran on Thursday accused the KDP of executing 25 PUK fighters.
